issues.finding: The contrast with a set-theoretic function writes its image as {f(x): x in A} for arbitrary A, without saying that f is defined on every member of A. A set-coded function may have a restricted domain; the displayed term f(x) requires the domain condition, even though the image of A intersected with the domain can be defined separately.
issues.proposed_resolution: Qualify the displayed f(x)-image expression by assuming f is defined on every member of the given A. The main Replacement scheme and its term-image corollary remain unchanged.

translation_treatment: The Javanese prose states the domain condition before the displayed set-function image. The source's distinction between a total syntactic term and a set-coded function, all formulas, and the double-union bounding footnote remain intact; frozen source bytes are unchanged.
